import mir_eval
import numpy as np

# Multipitch metrics require ragged arrays (list of 1D numpy arrays)
# Convert the provided 1D frequency arrays into ragged format
ref_time = np.arange(len(ref_freqs), dtype=float)
est_time = np.arange(len(est_freqs), dtype=float)

ref_ragged = [np.array([f]) if f > 0 else np.array([]) for f in ref_freqs]
est_ragged = [np.array([f]) if f > 0 else np.array([]) for f in est_freqs]

# Compute the 14-element tuple of multipitch metrics
metrics_tuple = mir_eval.multipitch.metrics(ref_time, ref_ragged, est_time, est_ragged)

# Compute self-metrics to establish a strong correctness oracle
self_metrics = mir_eval.multipitch.metrics(ref_time, ref_ragged, ref_time, ref_ragged)

assert len(metrics_tuple) == 14, f"Expected 14 metrics, got {len(metrics_tuple)}"

# When comparing identical data, precision and recall must be 1.0 (if there are any active pitches)
if any(len(arr) > 0 for arr in ref_ragged):
    assert self_metrics[0] == 1.0, f"Expected self-precision 1.0, got {self_metrics[0]}"
    assert self_metrics[1] == 1.0, f"Expected self-recall 1.0, got {self_metrics[1]}"
    assert self_metrics[2] == 1.0, f"Expected self-accuracy 1.0, got {self_metrics[2]}"

print(f"__CHECK__ metrics {len(metrics_tuple)}")
